- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- After sharp price spikes (≥10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent high.  
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is falling, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven support.  
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to forecast if sentiment is erratic.  
- If true outcome is below 70% of historical mean over 30d, model tends to be too optimistic; adjust downward by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- Forecast horizon >14d often shows lag; if sentiment is positive, add 1–2% to forecast for each additional day beyond 14d.
